gen-fs-quilon-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-m: Brushed-watercolor shifts in weight lead in Quilon, while Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono lays out clipped capitals with stencil-wide gaps. The sans body leaves open counters to breathe beside that display heading.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-comme: Editorial in tone, Quilon slims its joins yet stays sturdy. Comme then reads smoothly, a modern sans with no clogged curves and lowercase bodies filling most of the letter height, line after line.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-gidole: Gidole is a sans-serif drawn like neon tube, with a high midline and terminals held apart. Quilon, meanwhile, brings a soft stroke contrast that never turns flat or stark against that constant ink.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-heebo: Quilon carries an editorial, commanding presence, its strokes easing gently between fuller and slimmer. Heebo, a sans-serif, does the quieter job, with a tall central band and curves that stop short.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-hind-vadodara: A gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight defines Quilon. Hind Vadodara, a sans, holds a steady drafting-pen line and spacious terminal gaps below, so the heading's pen-like variation plays against it.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-huninn: Huninn is a modern sans built from monoline strokes. Beneath Quilon's gently shifting weight, Huninn's lowercase rises close to cap height and its s terminals stay clear, so paragraphs move along smoothly.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-julius-sans-one: Clean and approachable, Julius Sans One keeps one stroke thickness and wide gaps between letters. But Quilon handles the editorial drama with sensible stroke contrast, while the sans simply keeps the text open.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-kedebideri: Approachable, with a mild stroke contrast, Quilon leads. It does display best, while Kedebideri, a sans with rounded, inviting curves under a skyward x-height line, does the everyday text work.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-khula: Quilon moves in a soft cadence of fuller stems and slimmer links. Khula, a plain sans with a tall midsection and curves that hold their mouths open, gives that cadence a modern, quiet partner.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-krub: Editorial poise, built on modest weight shifts across every curve of Quilon. And Krub, a sans with pen-lifted curves and a pronounced x-height, carries long paragraphs forward without any fuss.
